options.text: The amount of oxygen used during exercise
The oxygen stored in the lungs
The extra oxygen needed after exercise to break down the lactic acid that accumulated during anaerobic respiration

questions.explanation: Oxygen debt (also called excess post-exercise oxygen consumption, EPOC) is the extra oxygen the body needs after exercise to metabolise the lactic acid that built up during anaerobic respiration.

questions.stem: Why does breathing remain elevated after exercise stops?

options.text: To cool the body down only
To continue supplying extra oxygen to repay the oxygen debt and break down lactic acid
The brain forgets to slow down breathing

questions.explanation: Breathing stays elevated after exercise to take in the extra oxygen needed to repay the oxygen debt: converting lactic acid back to glucose in the liver and restoring oxygen reserves.

questions.stem: Where is lactic acid transported to for breakdown?
questions.explanation: Lactic acid is transported in the blood to the liver, where it is converted back to glucose (which can be stored as glycogen) or fully oxidised to carbon dioxide and water.

questions.stem: What happens to lactic acid in the liver?

options.text: It is converted back to glucose or broken down using oxygen into CO2 and water

questions.explanation: In the liver, lactic acid is either converted back to glucose (which may be stored as glycogen) or oxidised with the extra oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water, releasing energy.

questions.stem: A person who has been sprinting will have a higher oxygen debt than someone who has been walking. Why?

options.text: Sprinting relies more heavily on anaerobic respiration, producing more lactic acid that needs to be broken down

questions.explanation: Sprinting is intense exercise that requires rapid energy release, leading to more anaerobic respiration and more lactic acid production. More oxygen is therefore needed afterwards to break down this lactic acid.

questions.stem: How long does it typically take to repay an oxygen debt after intense exercise?

options.text: Several minutes to over an hour, depending on the intensity

questions.explanation: Repaying the oxygen debt typically takes several minutes to over an hour. Heart rate and breathing rate remain elevated during this recovery period until all lactic acid has been metabolised.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of the oxygen debt recovery process?

options.text: Lactic acid conversion in the liver

questions.explanation: During recovery, lactic acid production decreases (not increases) as the body switches back to aerobic respiration. The elevated breathing and heart rate help deliver extra oxygen to break down existing lactic acid.
